candidates.headline: 4. AI企業集積地サンフランシスコ、データセンター新設の一時停止を決定（ブルームバーグ）2026/10/08
candidates.angle: Scale shift: the official 'temporary pause' is rendered visually tiny compared to the enormous existing datacenter campus, undercutting the decision's apparent weight.
candidates.title: 切手ほどの一時停止
candidates.scene: A vast campus of towering server buildings fills the background like a city skyline. In the foreground a municipal clerk sits at a folding table and presses a small rubber stamp labeled 'TEMPORARY PAUSE'. The stamped mark is postage-stamp-sized on the facade of a massive server tower visible behind him.
candidates.reason: 決定の言葉（声明）が、既に広がった物理的なインフラの規模に比べていかに小さく見えるかを強調することで、政策の実効性への皮肉を表現する。
candidates.visualTurn: A tiny 'TEMPORARY PAUSE' stamp impression is placed against a skyscraper-scale server façade, making the policy look minuscule in comparison to the built reality.
candidates.contradiction: The city's formal pause comes across as a minute administrative mark against sprawling datacenter infrastructure; the scale of words does not match the scale of what they aim to affect.
candidates.evidence: 4. AI企業集積地サンフランシスコ、データセンター新設の一時停止を決定（ブルームバーグ）2026/10/08

evaluation.reason: A very legible scale-contrast: a tiny municipal stamp versus an immense datacenter campus immediately undercuts the perceived weight of the policy. The ironic turn (administrative mark dwarfed by built reality) reads at a glance and would reproduce well at small sizes. But it implies the pause is merely symbolic or ineffective and presumes an existing campus of that enormous physical scale — neither claim is established by the headline.
unsupportedClaims: That there is already a sprawling, skyscraper-scale datacenter campus in San Francisco whose physical scale makes the pause negligible.
That the 'temporary pause' is only symbolic and will have no practical effect (the headline only says the pause may affect supply, not that it will be ineffective).

candidates.headline: 4. AI企業集積地サンフランシスコ、データセンター新設の一時停止を決定（ブルームバーグ）2026/10/08
candidates.angle: A literal role reversal: the infrastructure becomes the city's ruler and orders humans to stop construction, highlighting the paradox of an 'AI hub' halting data-center growth.
candidates.title: インフラが市長に
candidates.scene: On the steps of city hall, a towering server rack sits at a lectern wearing a mayoral sash and holding a gavel. Two human city officials and a small crew of construction workers stand before it, lowering their helmets and pausing work. Behind them a billboard reads "AI Hub".
candidates.reason: AI集積地としての誇りと、データセンター新設の一時停止という行動の矛盾を、権力の主体が人間から機械へ入れ替わる構図で強調する。
candidates.visualTurn: A server rack physically occupies the role of the mayor (sash, gavel, lectern) and gives the order; humans obey. The position of authority is reversed from people to machine.
candidates.contradiction: A city celebrated as an 'AI hub' visibly submits to a machine's command to halt expansion; the very infrastructure paradoxically enforces the slowdown it is supposed to enable.
candidates.evidence: 4. AI企業集積地サンフランシスコ、データセンター新設の一時停止を決定（ブルームバーグ）2026/10/08

evaluation.reason: Clear, immediate role-reversal: a server rack occupies the mayoral role and orders humans to halt construction, making the paradox visible without text. The image strongly registers an ironic contradiction between an 'AI hub' identity and a policy that pauses datacenter growth. However, it attributes agency or authority to infrastructure (machines) rather than to city officials, which is a metaphorical exaggeration not supported by the supplied headline.
unsupportedClaims: That the infrastructure (servers) actually acts as the city's decision-maker or issued the order to stop construction (implies machines caused the policy).
That the pause reflects a transfer of political authority from humans to machines.

candidates.headline: 4. AI企業集積地サンフランシスコ、データセンター新設の一時停止を決定（ブルームバーグ）2026/10/08
candidates.angle: Object inversion: the new data-center hardware is treated like a funerary object—pausing becomes burial, making the policy feel final and excessive.
candidates.title: 一時停止の葬儀
candidates.scene: A construction crane lowers a gleaming server rack into a freshly dug grave on a development site. A wreath with a ribbon reading 'temporary pause' leans against the pit. Several solemn workers stand with lowered heads and idle tools.
candidates.reason: 『一時停止』という行政措置を、成長の終焉として視覚化することで、その過剰さと皮肉を際立たせる。データセンターの新設がまるで葬式に見える対比を描く。
candidates.visualTurn: The server rack—normally a data-processing machine—is literally inverted into a coffin being buried, turning an object of growth into a funerary object in the image.
candidates.contradiction: A place defined by building computing capacity is shown burying the very hardware that enables it; a temporary administrative pause is depicted as a final burial.
candidates.evidence: 4. AI企業集積地サンフランシスコ、データセンター新設の一時停止を決定（ブルームバーグ）2026/10/08

evaluation.reason: The funeral/burial inversion makes the 'temporary pause' read as a final, excessive ending — a single, strong visual metaphor that contrasts a policy described as temporary with imagery of permanence. The scene communicates the ironic turn (growth → burial) clearly, but it asserts finality and categorical loss that the headline does not claim.
unsupportedClaims: That the 'temporary pause' is effectively a permanent termination (treating a pause as burial).
That the city is permanently ending data-center development rather than temporarily suspending approvals.

angleEvaluations.reason: Clear, immediate role-reversal: a server rack occupies the mayoral role and orders humans to halt construction, making the paradox visible without text. The image strongly registers an ironic contradiction between an 'AI hub' identity and a policy that pauses datacenter growth. However, it attributes agency or authority to infrastructure (machines) rather than to city officials, which is a metaphorical exaggeration not supported by the supplied headline.
unsupportedClaims: That the infrastructure (servers) actually acts as the city's decision-maker or issued the order to stop construction (implies machines caused the policy).
That the pause reflects a transfer of political authority from humans to machines.

angleEvaluations.reason: The funeral/burial inversion makes the 'temporary pause' read as a final, excessive ending — a single, strong visual metaphor that contrasts a policy described as temporary with imagery of permanence. The scene communicates the ironic turn (growth → burial) clearly, but it asserts finality and categorical loss that the headline does not claim.
unsupportedClaims: That the 'temporary pause' is effectively a permanent termination (treating a pause as burial).
That the city is permanently ending data-center development rather than temporarily suspending approvals.

angleEvaluations.reason: A very legible scale-contrast: a tiny municipal stamp versus an immense datacenter campus immediately undercuts the perceived weight of the policy. The ironic turn (administrative mark dwarfed by built reality) reads at a glance and would reproduce well at small sizes. But it implies the pause is merely symbolic or ineffective and presumes an existing campus of that enormous physical scale — neither claim is established by the headline.
unsupportedClaims: That there is already a sprawling, skyscraper-scale datacenter campus in San Francisco whose physical scale makes the pause negligible.
That the 'temporary pause' is only symbolic and will have no practical effect (the headline only says the pause may affect supply, not that it will be ineffective).

prompt:
Create a single editorial cartoon for English-speaking newspaper readers.
News headline (source evidence, not lettering): 4. AI企業集積地サンフランシスコ、データセンター新設の一時停止を決定（ブルームバーグ）2026/10/08
Satirical angle: Scale shift: the official 'temporary pause' is rendered visually tiny compared to the enormous existing datacenter campus, undercutting the decision's apparent weight.
Scene: A vast campus of towering server buildings fills the background like a city skyline. In the foreground a municipal clerk sits at a folding table and presses a small rubber stamp labeled 'TEMPORARY PAUSE'. The stamped mark is postage-stamp-sized on the facade of a massive server tower visible behind him.
Visual turn to show in the drawing: A tiny 'TEMPORARY PAUSE' stamp impression is placed against a skyscraper-scale server façade, making the policy look minuscule in comparison to the built reality.
Depict this visible ironic reversal, not a literal reenactment of the reported event or a generic portrait. The turn must read without the title. A metaphor must not assert an unreported action or guilt.
Deliver the illustration alone. The page layout adds its title separately as real text. Do not render any title, subtitle, caption, heading or footer anywhere in this image, including the white margins. Do not write any Japanese characters in the image. Do not add text beneath the figures.
Strongly reference the pen-and-ink editorial cartoon work of Georges Bigot, Charles Wirgman and Charles Keene: observant human caricature, expressive faces and gestures, lively economical contours with deliberate changes in line weight, convincing clothing folds, and sparse hand-drawn hatching. Make these nineteenth-century draughtsmen the primary visual references throughout the drawing.
Create the original artwork for a newspaper illustration that will be printed using letterpress equipment and techniques from 150 years ago, circa 1876. Draw a deliberately composed, human-looking pen-and-ink original for an engraver to turn into a relief printing block. Use economical, clearly separated lines that remain legible when printed at small column size. Deliver the clean original drawing, without simulated aged-paper or printed-ink texture. Specific recognizable characters, expressive caricature, one clear visual joke, spare composition, natural asymmetry, varied purposeful contour lines. Avoid generic AI illustration conventions, glossy perfection, decorative clutter, stock robot imagery unless the joke specifically needs it, and irrelevant objects.
Black ink strokes on pure white paper ONLY. Clear outlines; express every shadow with sparse hatching, cross-hatching or stippled marks. Leave white paper visible between strokes. No gray fills, gradients, smooth shading, color, digital painting, photorealism, artificial paper texture or engraving filter effect. Keep most areas unshaded. Compact square composition, width:height exactly 1:1, complete subjects within the frame.
Design for a small newspaper column only about 64 mm wide. Use one clear visual joke with no more than two main figures and one essential prop. Remove secondary people, inset maps, extra signs and ornamental detail. Prefer NO words inside the drawing. If the joke truly needs lettering, allow at most ONE speech bubble or label, no more than THREE short English words and 14 characters total. Make each capital letter at least 8% of the image height, bold and plainly readable at column size. Never add small lettering, uniform labels, evidence labels or background text, even if the proposed scene asks for them. These limits override any lettering and clutter requested in the scene. Do NOT draw the title, a caption, a border, watermark or signature inside the image; the title will be typeset separately. Treat the scene as satire, and do not invent additional factual allegations beyond the supplied headline.
